newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish tea exports weak despite stocks - report.
newsitem.headline: Turkish tea exports weak despite stocks - report.

text.p: Turkish tea exports remain at considerably low levels without the means of competing with the world's top tea exporters, despite higher output and rising stocks, a report prepared by the Turkish treasury said.

It said Turkey's private tea producers and state-run Cay-Kur were forced to raise their exports in recent years due to growing stocks, but "differences in taste" in export markets and higher production costs were the main handicaps in tea exports.
Turkey is expected to realize a total of 44,000 tonnes of tea exports this year to Netherlands, Poland and Russia.

"Although Turkey is among the world's biggest tea producers and consumers, it was not able to get sustainable share from the world market. Between years 1990 and 1995, Turkey's tea exports were about 10 percent of its total output," the report said.
Turkey was the world's sixth biggest tea producer with 145,000 tonnes of dry tea in 1995 and it consumed about five percent of world's total dry tea output.

The yearly average domestic black tea consumption is around 140,000 tonnes of which Cay-Kur meets 61 percent and private companies 28 percent while the remaining 11 percent is imported or smuggled in for better quality.
"Cay-Kur is buying more tea leaves from farmers than needed to support them and excess harvest creates stockpiles with high running costs," the report said.
The report said imported and smuggled tea due to consumer preferences was another reason behind the piling of domestically produced tea.

Average yearly tea imports range between 1,000 and 2,000 tonnes, mainly from Sri Lanka. But about 10,000 tonnes of dry tea is estimated to enter Turkey via smuggling each year from its southeastern regions.
The report said Turkey's dry tea production is expected to stay at between 130,000-140,000 tonnes per year by 2000.
Cay-Kur, one of Turkey's biggest state-run companies, has made sales worth $231 million last year and had 103,000 tonnes of tea stocks at end-1995. -- Istanbul newsroom +90-312-446 29 40
